D-68.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a regular customer (not flagged), with one asset.
  • Have a new billable work order for the regular customer, not invoiced, with two lines: each with 1.0 h of labor and one stock part with a cost, made for this test.
  • Mark the second line No Charge with the category Warranty.
  • Open the attached pictures iwo-flow6-03-03-line-marked-no-charge-0-00.png, iwo-happy-32-32-line-marked-no-charge-0-00.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.3 (12 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-12226 (Story 12, A no-charge line on a billable work order)

  • S12-R3: “A no-charge line shows the chip "No Charge · [category]" next to its title on the lines table, in Tech View and on mobile; Rate, Total and every part on it show $0.00; Margin shows nothing. Hours, technician, status, approval, parts ordering, picking, receiving, clock-ins, notes, inspections and the story work as on any line. The original work order and line are not shown on the line; they are in the notes, the Audit Log, the report and the hub record.”
  • S12-R4: “The work order carries no badge and no header style and its classification stays billable; Financial Info (the cost view) does not change. Totals, tax, work order fees and discounts, deposits, the estimate, the portal approval and the Customer PO are computed on the billable lines; the no-charge line shows at $0.00 on the estimate and in the portal with its category under the title. A line discount on the line is removed when it is marked and not restored by Mark as Billable. A deposit on the work order does not block the mark; when, after the mark, the deposit exceeds the billable total, the dialog says "Deposit $[amount] exceeds the new total $[total]. The difference stays on the customer's account as a deposit when the invoice is created." and the existing rule applies at invoicing. An estimate already on the portal shows the live work order when the customer opens it (same link, no new email; the advisor re-sends when a fresh document is wanted), with the line at $0.00 and its category under the title and the notice "This estimate changed after it was sent. The lines above are current."; a pending IBS request is not withdrawn (ShopView has no withdrawal); as after any price change today, the advisor requests approval again with the new amount when needed. ShopView renders the estimate and invoice documents and the portal shows them; the portal renders its own approval line cards, price summary and emails, where the $0.00 line shows with its category: that portal side is its own story, SV-12296, linked to SV-12226.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “No-charge line | "No Charge · [category]" | Chip next to the line title; Rate, Total and parts at $0.00; Margin empty (S12-R3)”
  • Terminology: “No Charge line → a line of a billable work order marked No Charge with a category. It shows $0.00 on the work order, the estimate, the portal and the invoice; its hours, parts and story stay; its parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created. The work order carries no badge.”
  • Key Decisions: “A no-charge line stays on its billable work order and shows $0.00 on one invoice, instead of moving to a separate work order. One work order, one classification, one document still holds for whole internal and no-charge work orders; the line case is the exception and is handled line by line in the invoice, the posting and every report.”
  • S2-R3: “The work order header shows one badge next to the status: "Internal" for an internal work order, "No Charge" for a no-charge work order (a different style from Internal), in the desktop and the mobile header. It is the only mark on the work order: the customer card on the detail page shows no badge and no category. On the detail page the header card of an internal or no-charge work order has an orange outline and a light orange background (a new style for the header card, on desktop and on the mobile header; the design authority names the token), so the work order is recognised at a glance; there is no hint sentence under the header. The category of a no-charge work order is not shown on the work order; it is in the Change category dialog, on the NO CHARGE document and in the report (S2-R16). A billable work order that carries no-charge lines carries no badge and no header style; the line carries the mark (Story 12).”
